title: pravapis stem inventory row
description: The etymology inventory (data/lexicon/stems/*.tsv): one row per stem, answering the one question the spelling cannot — is this stem a Western borrowing? NORMATIVE for any implementation. The file is TSV, so this schema describes (a) the file dialect, in `x-tsv`, and (b) the object each data line parses into, in `$defs/row`. A validator reads `x-tsv.columns` to split the line, then validates the object.

declaration.description: Every stems file must declare, in its first non-blank lines, the schema it is written against and the column order it uses. Directives are comments, so existing readers skip them, but a validator refuses a file that does not declare. This is what makes the column order a fact about the file rather than a fact about the parser.

columns.example: #!columns stem	class	alternations	source	provenance	target
columns.description: Must list the columns below, in order. Trailing optional columns may be omitted only if no row uses them.

columns.name: stem
columns.description: The stem, lowercase. A leading '-' marks it UNANCHORED — it may match anywhere in the word rather than only at the start, which is how -логі reaches біялогія without also claiming падлогі. The '-' is a flag, not part of the stem.

columns.name: class
columns.description: Etymology, as far as the loanword rules care.

columns.name: alternations
columns.description: Comma-separated alternation codes this stem licenses, or a null token. A code may carry a direction restriction, written code:n2t or code:t2n, for an alternation that is derivable one way and ambiguous the other (салон → салён is safe; салёны → салоны is not).

columns.name: source
columns.description: Where the classification comes from: a section of the codification, or a named dictionary. Surfaced on every change record as `citation`. A null token means unsourced, which `cited` provenance forbids.

columns.name: provenance
columns.description: How the row got here. `uncertain` rows are parsed, counted and NEVER applied — the inventory records doubt instead of deleting it.

columns.name: target
columns.description: Escape hatch: the Taraškievica form outright, for stems the regular alternations cannot derive (каланіял → калёніял restores an etymological о that akanne wrote as а, which no rule conditioned on the Narkamaŭka spelling can know). Prefer `alternations`.

stem.description: Lowercased, NFC-normalised, with the unanchored '-' flag removed.

anchored.description: False when the raw stem began with '-'. An anchored stem matches only as a prefix of the word.

forward_only.description: The subset of `alternations` written with an :n2t restriction — applied Narkamaŭka → Taraškievica only.

allOf.title: A native stem licenses nothing
allOf.description: It makes no claim about the codification — it says the word is ordinary Belarusian vocabulary, which is precisely what makes the loanword rules leave it alone.

allOf.title: A cited loan must say where from
An applied loan must be able to fire
allOf.description: A loan stem with neither alternations nor a target changes nothing, so it is dead weight that reads as coverage.

allOf.title: forward_only is a subset of alternations

description: A stems file, parsed: the ordered list of its data rows.
x-constraints: Longest match wins. A word resolves against the longest stem that matches it, anchored beating unanchored on a tie. This is how false friends are handled: native `класц` beats loan `клас` on класці, so no rule needs a lookahead.
(stem, anchored) is the primary key. Duplicates are an error, not a last-one-wins.
Rows whose provenance is `uncertain` are loaded and counted but never applied.
